steps.name: Depth & outlier assessment of sample_01
steps.question: Is sample_01 (AD skin treated/control design, 6 vs 6) merely shallow (~4x below median library size) or an outlier that threatens the treated-vs-control comparison?
steps.description: Load /eval-four-models-v2-without-python-two-group-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata.csv; quantify library sizes and diagnose sample_01, whose library is ~4x below the median. Compute per-sample total counts, genes detected, and the size factors PyDESeq2 would assign; plot PCA on log2(CPM+1) to check whether sample_01 clusters with its condition group or is a within-group outlier, and whether depth drives PC1. Decide and document handling: retain all samples in the primary DE (size-factor normalization of the negative binomial model accommodates 4x depth differences) and run a drop-sample_01 sensitivity analysis downstream; escalate to exclusion only if PCA shows sample_01 as a condition-defying outlier rather than merely shallow. Apply a standard low-count pre-filter (e.g. genes with count >= 10 in at least 6 samples) and record retained gene counts.
acceptance_criteria: Library sizes computed for all 12 samples; sample_01 quantified relative to the median and its condition confirmed from metadata.csv

Counts matrix parsed correctly (12,000 genes x 12 samples; first column is the gene identifier) and sample sheet joined without mismatches
A written handling decision: primary DE keeps all 12 samples with size-factor normalization; sample_01 additionally flagged for a drop-one sensitivity run
Pre-filtering rule (e.g. count threshold keeping genes with adequate counts across samples) recorded with the retained gene count

steps.name: Treated vs control DE with PyDESeq2
steps.question: Which genes change between treated and control in AD skin, and which of those calls survive removal of shallow sample_01?
steps.description: Differential expression of treated vs control on the filtered counts from T1S1 using PyDESeq2 (Wald test, unpaired design ~condition, Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment). Primary fit uses all 12 samples with median-of-ratios size factors. Detect the gene identifier space in counts.csv; if the identifiers are not HGNC symbols, map them via the staged UniProt human ID mapping table (Ensembl gene/protein columns) to HGNC symbols for downstream pathway work, collapsing multi-mapped entries by keeping the gene with the largest |statistic|. Produce the full results table (baseMean, log2FC, shrunken LFC if available, Wald statistic, p-value, padj) and a significant list (padj < 0.05 plus an |LFC| threshold, stated explicitly). Sensitivity: rerun the identical fit without sample_01 and report overlap of significant genes, Spearman correlation of gene-level statistics between the two fits, and whether any top genes change direction. This dual run is what 'handle sample_01 carefully' means at the gene level.
acceptance_criteria: PyDESeq2 fit on all 12 samples with design = condition (treated vs control), unpaired; convergence confirmed
Results table written with gene ID, HGNC symbol (mapped if counts are Ensembl/other), baseMean, log2FC, lfcSE, Wald statistic, p-value, padj (Benjamini-Hochberg)
Significant-gene list defined as padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1 (thresholds recorded), split by direction
Sensitivity rerun without sample_01 completed; concordance reported: number of significant genes shared, Spearman correlation of Wald statistics, and any direction flips for top genes
Shrunken LFC (apeglm-style) produced for the primary fit if supported by the installed pydeseq2 version
Explicit statement of which genes are robust to sample_01 and which depend on it

steps.name: Hallmark GSEA on DE ranking
steps.question: Which MSigDB hallmark pathways are shifted between treated and control AD skin, and do the calls hold when sample_01 is dropped?
steps.description: Hallmark pathway analysis from the DE ranking. Build a ranked list (sign(statistic) x -log10(p), or the Wald statistic, stated in the output) from the T1S2 primary fit, restricted to genes that survived pre-filtering and mapped to HGNC symbols (duplicates collapsed by keeping the max |score|). Run gseapy.prerank against the staged MSigDB human hallmark GMT (h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, 50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols) fully offline from the local file. Report ES, NES, nominal p, and FDR q for all 50 sets, with leading-edge genes for significant sets (q < 0.25, the GSEA convention). Rerun the prerank on the no-sample_01 statistics and report which hallmark sets are robust vs dependent on the shallow sample. As a complement, run over-representation (gseapy.enrich with the same local GMT) on the up- and down-regulated significant gene lists with a documented minimum/maximum set size, so genes-only and rank-based views of 'which hallmark pathways change' can be compared.
acceptance_criteria: Ranking file built from T1S2 primary statistics (all 12 samples), genes mapped to HGNC symbols, one row per unique symbol
gseapy.prerank GSEA completed against the local MSigDB 2026.1 human hallmark GMT (50 HALLMARK_* sets); no network calls
ES, NES, nominal p, and FDR q reported for all 50 sets; sets passing q < 0.25 (GSEA convention) listed with their leading-edge genes
Sensitivity rerun without sample_01 completed; hallmark sets compared (NES sign, rank shift); any set whose significance depends on sample_01 flagged
ORA of up- and down-regulated significant genes against the same hallmark GMT as a complementary view, with gene-set size filters stated
Sorted enrichment results written to CSV/TSV for the report

plan.title: AD skin DE (PyDESeq2) + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is human skin bulk RNA-seq (12,000 genes x 12 samples, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) with gene-level Salmon counts in counts.csv and a 12-row metadata.csv. The question is which genes and which MSigDB hallmark pathways change between treated and control, with explicit care for sample_01, whose library size is ~4x below the median. The plan has two tracks. Track 1 does a depth/outlier assessment of sample_01 (is it merely shallow or also a condition/outlier problem), then a two-group differential-expression analysis in PyDESeq2 on all 12 samples — size-factor normalization is the statistically correct way to handle uneven depth, so the primary analysis keeps every sample — plus a sensitivity rerun excluding sample_01 to show which findings depend on it. Track 2 converts the DE statistic into a ranked gene list, maps identifiers to HGNC symbols, and runs rank-based GSEA against the staged MSigDB human hallmark GMT (2026.1, 50 sets), again with and without sample_01, so the pathway answer carries the same sensitivity check. Everything is Python: pydeseq2, pandas/numpy, scikit-learn, gseapy. No R.
